analysis:
On 31 January 2024 Shah's office posted that not a single incident of stone-pelting took place in Jammu and Kashmir in 2023. PTI reported the statement.

Official data support the statement for the category actually counted. An MHA compilation reported by TOI recorded 'nil' organised hartals and organised stone-pelting linked to terrorism and separatism up to 15 December 2023, against 52 hartals and 1,221 stone-pelting incidents in 2018. A Rajya Sabha reply in July 2024 said there had been no organised stone-pelting or organised hartal since 2023, and NDTV reported MHA data showing a 100% drop from 2,654 incidents in 2010.

The claim is exact only under the 'organised' qualifier: sporadic stone-throwing has occurred in other years, including a protest in Srinagar in March 2026 that the Indian Express described as the first such protest since 2019. Because the claim is specifically about 2023 and the official 2023 record is nil, it is recorded as true with the qualifier noted.
notes: The wording is from PTI/The Week and refers to a post by Shah's office, so quote_is_verbatim is false. The primary MHA document was not opened; the figures come via TOI/NDTV/Akashvani reporting of MHA and Rajya Sabha replies. The literal phrasing ('not a single incident') is broader than the official 'organised' category; a reviewer may prefer 'misleading' if sporadic incidents within 2023 are documented.
